3) Expected retention/monitoring window for logs/telemetry?

Camila  thanks for the recap and the spreadsheet. A few quick answers and follow-ups from our side:

- Scope: yes, Aurora will be sending PHI (clinical notes) from production EHR-derived pipelines. This is core to the evaluation.
- BAA: Aurora requires a signed BAA in place for any vendor processing PHI  that will be handled by procurement/legal.

Requesting the following from Redwood to proceed:
1) Current SOC 2 status (Type II preferred) and a redacted report or SOC summary.
2) Confirmation of encryption in transit and at rest, plus key management options (do you support customer-managed keys / BYOK?).
3) Subprocessor list and notification cadence for changes.
4) Network architecture diagram and details on VPC peering options (if any).
5) Data residency: can you guarantee processing and storage in US-only regions?

Procurement will own the SIG completion; I cc'd them. Our procurement lead (Sarah Lee) will reach out if they need additional steps.

Thanks  can you send the SOC summary and network diagram? We may also ask for an NDA/NDA addendum before sharing the detailed SOC report.

Best,
Alex Johnson

Aurora Health

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire initiation - Aurora Health

Alex  great, thanks for the clarity. Answers below and a couple clarifying questions so we can fill the SIG accurately.

Answered items:
- SOC 2: Redwood has completed SOC 2 Type II for our hosted inference platform (report period ended June 2027). I've attached a one-page SOC summary (redwood_soc2_summary.pdf). We can share the full report under NDA.
- Encryption: yes  TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest. For hosting: in our Hosted API we manage keys; for Private (VPC/onprem) deployments we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS).
- Subprocessors: we maintain a posted list and will provide the current roster; we also provide 30-day minimum notice for changes (we'll include the link in the SIG).
- Network diagram: attached (network-diagram.pdf). For hosted customers, we do not offer direct VPC peering for the multi-tenant hosted product. Dedicated/Private options do support VPC connectivity.
- Data residency: we can restrict processing to US regions for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted API customers we have regional controls and can prioritize US-only regions  we'll note this in the SIG.

Clarifying questions for Aurora (so we can answer the SIG fields correctly):
1) Confirm whether Aurora intends to use Redwood's Hosted API (multi-tenant) or pursue a Dedicated/Private deployment for production PHI.
2) Does Aurora require active log retention beyond 90 days (security logs/recordings)? If so, what retention window?
3) Any specific compliance requirements beyond HIPAA (e.g., state-level controls, HITRUST)?

Next steps / attachments:
- Attached: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, network-diagram.pdf
- I will start populating SIG-v1.xlsx with the answers we can confirm today and mark items needing legal/NDA for redacted SOC report.
- Proposed follow-up: Mon, Aug 23 at 10:00 AM PT to review outstanding items and coordinate with procurement. Does that work for you and Sarah?

If procurement prefers, we can route the BAA via DocuSign  I can share the link once procurement confirms contact.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
